title.narrative: Life-Saving Unconditional Cash Assistance to Improve Immediate Food Access for Vulnerable Drought-Affected Households in Burhakaba District, Bay Region, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project seeks to improve immediate access to food for drought-affected villages in Burhakaba District, Bay Region, Somalia, which has been severely impacted by the failure of the 2025 Deyr rains and the ongoing Jilaal dry season. These climatic shocks have resulted in widespread crop failure, loss of livelihoods, increased market dependency, and reduced purchasing power among poor and vulnerable households, particularly those classified under IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) and IPC Phase 4 (Emergency). In Burhakaba District an estimated 74,189 indiduals are under stress, 43,722 classified as in crisis and 14,377 in emergency situation, this is according to Somalia 2025 Post Gu IPC AFI Analyses Population Estimates and Classification.The overall objective of the project is to meet the immediate food needs of the most vulnerable households through the provision of life-saving Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT). Cash assistance has been selected as the most appropriate response modality as local markets in Burhakaba remain functional, and cash enables households to access food according to their priority needs while preserving dignity and choice.ltbrgtThe intervention will target households in IPC Phase 3 and 4 areas of Burhakaba District, with a strong focus on female-headed households, households with children under five, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and displaced households. Y-PEER Somalia will apply the Community-Based Targeting (CBT) Guidelines for Somalia, combining vulnerability criteria with community validation to ensure transparent, inclusive, and accountable beneficiary selection. Prior to registration, community engagement and sensitization meetings will be conducted in each targeted village to explain project objectives, eligibility criteria, entitlements, and complaints mechanisms.ltbrgtThe cash transfer value is informed by the September 2025 Somalia Cash Working Group recommendations and aligned with Food Security Cluster guidance. Each selected household will receive USD 55 per month, covering approximately 70% of the food Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), for a total of three consecutive rounds during February, March, and April 2026. This period coincides with the peak of the drought and anticipated humanitarian assistance pipeline breaks, making timely support critical.ltbrgtThrough this intervention, 1811 vulnerable households (approximately 10,866 individuals) will be reached with unconditional cash assistance. The project will be implemented across selected villages in Burhakaba District, with household allocation per village determined through community-based targeting and validation processes to reflect severity of need and population size. Y-PEER will target 7 villages in the District as follows:lt/pgtltpgtAfar Golay, 307lt/pgtltpgtBalow 386lt/pgtltpgtAw Ooyaw 306lt/pgtltpgtKuraw Aw Riikaw 229lt/pgtltpgtAw Macaliin Foge 217lt/pgtltpgtLibooti 237 lt/pgtltpgtDhiigdaare 229lt/pgtltpgtAll beneficiary households will have a registered sim card to facilitate secure and efficient mobile money transfers. Cash registration and verification will be conducted by trained Y-PEER field teams using standardized registration tools and the Single Registration Form to minimize duplication and errors. Cash transfers will be delivered through reliable mobile money service providers operating in the district.ltbrgtThroughout implementation, Y-PEER Somalia will closely coordinate with district authorities, Area-Based Coordination structures, the Food Security Cluster, and other humanitarian partners at district and regional levels. This coordination will ensure complementarity with other interventions, avoid duplication, support referrals to other services where needed, and contribute to a coherent, area-based drought response in Burhakaba District.lt/pgt
